long_biography.plain_text:
Retail entrepreneur Brett Blundy learned the importance of location from a failing record shop in Pakenham. He and a friend bought the business, then took outside jobs to cover its losses. After days unloading hay or bunching carrots, he delivered customers' music orders at night. A second shop in a busy shopping centre performed much better.

In northern Australia, he backed cattle businesses that needed better access to water. At Beetaloo Station, he financed the Dunnicliff family's programme of tanks and troughs, allowing cattle to graze more of the property. He also funded bore-water pipelines at Amungee Mungee, where station managers Adrian and Emma Brown held a minority stake and supervised development.
